transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-24
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Priya Nair (Redwood AE), Diego Martinez (Redwood SE), Rachel Kim (AstraCart Head of ML), Tom Higgins (SVP Eng), Anika Bose (FinOps), Victor Lee (SRE)

Summary:
Quick QBR/check-in focused on upcoming Q2 pilot readiness: usage growth trends, cost hotspots (embeddings + tail GPT calls), reliability targets (p95/p99), and networking/security for a VPC-enabled pilot. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send security docs and run short performance benchmark; AstraCart to confirm pilot endpoints and budget.

Topics covered:
- Current usage and burst patterns
- Cost breakdown and embedding-heavy pages
- Latency / tail latency incidents and mitigation options
- Dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs (predictability vs ops ownership)
- VPC/private deployment networking and KMS/encryption concerns
- Pilot scope and metrics for success

Transcript body:
[00:00] Priya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I see all the names, appreciate the time. Quick note, Diego will handle the performance detail, I’ll run the commercial/security bits.
[00:30] Rachel: Perfect, thanks. We want to focus on two things today: controlling our embed spend and getting the p99 down on checkout predictions.
[01:05] Tom: yes, we had a 9-minute outage last week but more annoying were the 600ms p99 spikes on the price-recalc endpoint.
[01:30] Diego: ok, so from our side we looked at the traces you shared. The spikes line up with long prefix lengths and a big batch flush — looks like intermittent batching backpressure.
[02:10] Victor: yep, that’s our read pattern — sudden surge when a campaign triggers thousands of cart updates.
[02:35] Priya: good color. On the cost side Anika, can you summarize what’s worrying you this quarter?
[02:50] Anika: embeddings are the main driver — product search vectors grew 3x and embeddings are coming through our pipeline unnecessarily for some cold traffic. So cost per session has doubled in two months.
[03:20] Priya: understood, we typically recommend prefix caching + deduping for cold traffic and selectively using low-dim embeddings for exploratory queries to save units.
[03:50] Rachel: when you say low-dim embeddings, do you mean model-switching or quantized embeddings?
[04:05] Diego: both are options. We can route high-signal traffic to the larger embedding model and low-signal to a 512-dim cheaper variant. Also we have a cache tier that avoids re-embedding identical queries.
[04:40] Tom: sounds promising. For the spikes, what’s the simplest change we can test in the pilot to reduce p99?
[04:58] Diego: continuous batching tweaks and a small decrease in max batch wait (we can trade a few ms median latency for far fewer huge batches causing tail issues). Also prioritize key endpoints — prioritization token.
[05:25] Victor: will that hurt throughput for bulk jobs, like nightly indexing?
[05:40] Diego: bulk jobs you can route to dedicated capacity windows or separate queue, so it doesn't interfere.
[06:05] Priya: high-level deployment choices: you asked earlier about dedicated vs hosted — dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity and predictable p99, hosted is faster to start but tail might be less predictable at peak. For AstraCart’s needs, a short dedicated pilot for the two critical endpoints is worth testing.
[06:40] Anika: dedicated seems right for predictable billing too. We need cost predictability for the Q2 marketing push.
[07:00] Rachel: security is a must — we need VPC peering and KMS control. Can Redwood support customer-managed keys?
[07:20] Priya: yes, in Redwood Private we support customer KMS/HSM integration; in Dedicated we also offer VPC/network peering and private endpoints. We’ll send the detailed architecture diagram.
[07:45] Tom: great, and what about audit logs and retention? We need at least 12 months with SSO/SAML integration.
[08:00] Priya: SOC2 + audit logs are standard in enterprise tier; SSO/SAML is supported and we can configure long-term retention as an add-on. I’ll include exact retention SLAs in the pack.
[08:30] Rachel: re: pilot metrics — can we define success as p99 < 500ms for price-recalc and embed cost per 1k sessions down 30%?
[08:55] Priya: yes, that’s concrete. Diego, can you scope the benchmark?
[09:10] Diego: I’ll do a mixed traffic replay: 70% interactive low-token, 20% medium multi-turn, 10% bulk embeddings. I’ll run it for 48 hours on a config that mirrors production traffic.
[09:35] Anika: and billing measurement? We need to see token & embedding unit breakdown per route.
[09:50] Diego: we’ll produce token-level billing breakdown and per-endpoint latency percentiles.
[10:05] Victor: network constraints — we plan to peer from GCP us-east, and we need region affinity, do you support regional placement?
[10:25] Priya: yes, we can pin to region and have fallbacks; we’ll note the primary region and a secondary for failover.
[10:45] Tom: any data residency concerns for EU customers? Not for our current pilot but planning ahead.
[11:00] Priya: got it — we support region-specific deployments and can ensure data stays within region for Private deployments.
[11:25] Rachel: what about model rollouts? We want canary before full switch.
[11:40] Diego: built-in rollout controls: canary %, automatic rollback on quality regressions. We can attach eval sets to monitor outputs.
[12:00] Anika: quality monitoring tied to our prompt set is critical — we don’t want cost reduction to degrade recommendation quality.
[12:20] Priya: agree — we’ll instrument evals and set threshold alerts.
[12:40] Rachel: ok, fiscal question: for the two-week pilot what are the typical committed rates or is it pay-as-you-go?
[12:55] Priya: short pilots usually run on pay-as-you-go with a small trial credit; dedicated reserved pricing starts once you commit monthly. I’ll include a pilot-friendly pricing table.
[13:20] Tom: and SLAs during pilot?
[13:30] Priya: we provide 99% basic uptime for hosted pilots; dedicated pilot can have elevated SLOs — we’ll call that out.
[13:50] Victor: Diego, do you expect any configuration changes on our side for the VPC peering?
[14:05] Diego: will need an ingress CIDR and a nat rule for egress to our model runtime endpoints; also an IAM role for KMS access if customer-managed keys are used. I’ll list the exact steps.
[14:35] Rachel: what about observability — token-level traces and cost attribution per route?
[14:50] Diego: Console provides token-level cost, per-route latency and tracing hooks; we can also stream raw traces to your S3 for internal analytics.
[15:10] Anika: streaming is important for our finance team.
[15:25] Priya: noted.
[15:40] Rachel: can Redwood help with prompt tuning to reduce token counts?
[15:55] Diego: yes, we offer prompt engineering recommendations and model selection guidance; Optimize tooling can suggest quantization and batching params to reduce unit cost.
[16:20] Tom: how often do you suggest we re-evaluate batching config?
[16:35] Diego: after any traffic change; for a big campaign we normally revisit within 48 hours. The Optimize tool also pushes suggestions as traffic evolves.
[16:55] Rachel: any gotchas with embedding caches and consistency? We sometimes have stale vectors after real-time product updates.
[17:15] Diego: caching is prefix-based and supports TTL invalidation hooks; for real-time updates we recommend an event-driven invalidation pipeline.
[17:40] Victor: ok, we’ll need the webhook spec.
[17:50] Priya: we’ll include that in the security/ops pack.
[18:05] Rachel: timeline — can we start the pilot first week of May?
[18:20] Priya: yes, if you provide endpoints and traffic profile by 2025-04-30 we can stand up dedicated pilot the week of 2025-05-05.
[18:40] Anika: budget approval is pending but likely to be greenlight with the numbers you’ll send.
[19:00] Priya: action items recap in chat: I’ll send SOC2, arch diagram, pilot pricing, and Diego will run benchmark and share traces.
[19:20] Tom: any legal/contract prelims we should start?
[19:35] Priya: we can share a pilot MSA template; for dedicated commitments we’ll move to a contract.
[19:50] Victor: one more operational: what’s your rollback cadence for model failures?
[20:05] Diego: automatic rollback on latency or quality thresholds plus manual rollback via Console; we can set a canary window of X minutes.
[20:25] Rachel: fine.
[20:35] Priya: ok, anything else?
[20:40] Rachel: just one thing — can you include an example billing run so Anika can see a real example line item?
[20:55] Anika: yes please.
[21:05] Priya: will do.
[21:15] Diego: quick note — we spotted a possible optimization: switching the price-recalc endpoint to a streaming token model reduces peak memory and can shave p99 significantly, but it requires minor client changes.
[21:40] Tom: how minor?
[21:50] Diego: a small streaming client change to accept early tokens and a slight async handler; we can provide SDK snippets.
[22:10] Victor: ok, add that as a dev item.
[22:20] Priya: adding to action items.
[22:30] Rachel: great.
[22:40] Priya: if no other items, I’ll summarize and we’ll follow up with the pack.
[22:50] Tom: sounds good.
[23:00] Anika: thanks everyone.
[23:10] Rachel: thanks.

(Notes: transcription includes a few small mis-hearings; some product names may be truncated in audio. Periodic timestamps above every ~30-90s.)

End of transcript.
